subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic stalled-subagent recovery now, and should it live as default runtime nudge-to-kill behavior or be folded into the sessions.activity/watchdog design?
rationale: The remaining work changes default child-run termination behavior, adds or alters config/API surfaces, and defines parent/channel-visible failure semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve runtime recovery contract
options.body: Implement deterministic subagent activity tracking with conservative default or opt-out thresholds, nudge-to-kill behavior, parent/channel terminal delivery, and focused upgrade/docs/tests.

options.title: Fold into sessions.activity/watchdog
options.body: Keep this issue open as a requirement of #39127/#39141 so recovery and alerts share one activity state model before kill behavior lands.

options.title: Keep current mitigations
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds, diagnostics, and admin/manual kill paths while accepting the current silent-stall UX gap.

recommendation.title: Approve runtime recovery contract
recommendation.body: Implement deterministic subagent activity tracking with conservative default or opt-out thresholds, nudge-to-kill behavior, parent/channel terminal delivery, and focused upgrade/docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work is closest to subagent timeout math, stale-run cleanup, and admin session kill semantics, which are the central product boundaries for this decision.
